title: BACE: Biotechnology Skills (Practical) - Biotechnology Skills - Micropipetting
subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which micropipette is most appropriate for measuring a volume of 150 µL?
questions.explain: The P200 pipet typically covers the range of 20–200 µL. 150 µL falls perfectly within this range.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q:
A P20 micropipette display reads the following from top to bottom:
**1**
**2**
**5** (Red)

What volume is set?
questions.explain: On a P20, the top digit is tens, the middle is ones, and the bottom (red) is tenths. Thus, 1-2-5 represents 12.5 µL.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q:
A P200 micropipette display reads:
**0**
**5**
**0**

What volume is set?
questions.explain: On a P200, the digits are Hundreds, Tens, Ones. 0-5-0 reads as 050 µL, which is 50 µL.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q:
A P1000 micropipette display reads:
**0** (Red)
**5**
**0**

What volume is set?
questions.explain: On a P1000, the top (red) digit is Thousands (mL), the middle is Hundreds, and the bottom is Tens. 0-5-0 reads as 050 tens, or 500 µL.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: When aspirating (drawing up) liquid, you should depress the plunger to which position?
options: All the way down to the plastic body
Halfway between the first and second stop
questions.explain: You push to the **first stop** to aspirate the calibrated volume. Pushing to the second stop before entering the liquid will draw up too much volume.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'second stop' on a micropipette?
options: To draw up the liquid accurately.
To purge or blow out the remaining liquid during dispensing.
questions.explain: The second stop is used only during dispensing to blow out the last drop of liquid from the tip, ensuring accurate delivery.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Why is it important to release the plunger slowly after aspirating liquid?
options: To prevent aerosols and liquid from splashing into the pipette shaft.
To heat the liquid via friction.
To ensure the second stop is engaged.
questions.explain: Snapping the plunger back can cause liquid to splash up into the internal shaft, contaminating the pipette and damaging the piston.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which pipette would be the **most accurate** choice to measure 2.5 µL?
questions.explain: A P20 (range 2–20 µL) is the correct choice. P200 and P1000 cannot accurately measure such small volumes.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the lower limit of effective accuracy for a standard P200 micropipette?
questions.explain: A P200 generally has a functional range of 20 µL to 200 µL. Below 20 µL, a P20 should be used for better accuracy.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which part of the pipette is disposable and must be changed between samples?
questions.explain: The plastic tip is the only disposable part that touches the liquid.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: If a P20 pipette reads **1-0-0** (Top-Middle-Bottom [red]), what is the volume?
questions.explain: P20: Top=10s (1), Middle=1s (0), Bottom=0.1s (0). Total = 10.0 µL.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Before using a micropipette, you should always check:
options: That the volume is set within the specified range of the pipette.
That the pipette has been autoclaved.
That the tip ejector is removed.
questions.explain: Adjusting a pipette outside its designated range (e.g., above 200µL on a P200) can damage the internal mechanism and lead to inaccurate measurements.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills
